title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
authors: A. Razanajatovo, J. Cayssol, C. Dutreix
abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. This establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structures in scanning tunneling microscopy using conventional, unpolarized tips.
summary: This paper introduces a novel tomography technique to extract detailed electronic properties, such as the density matrix and Quantum Geometric Tensor, from standard STM QPI maps. By exploiting crystal symmetries, the method resolves orbital contributions that are otherwise averaged out by unpolarized tips. This breakthrough establishes impurities as powerful probes for mapping band structures in honeycomb materials.
main_problem: The goal is to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states and the quantum geometric tensor (QGT) from quasiparticle interference (QPI) maps obtained using conventional, unpolarized scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) tips.
main_result: The method successfully establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structures, allowing the reconstruction of the full density matrix and QGT directly from unpolarized LDOS measurements.
method: It utilizes a tomography approach based on exploiting the symmetry properties (point group representations) of scattering states to disentangle orbital contributions within the total measured LDOS modulation.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on two-orbital models defined on a honeycomb lattice, relevant for graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. The low-energy physics is described by a $2 	imes 2$ Hamiltonian $\hat{H}(\mathbf{k})$.
key_observables: Density matrix ($\hat{\rho}$), orbital populations ($P_\alpha$), quantum coherence ($C_{BA}$), Quantum Metric (Re[QGT]), and Berry Curvature (Im[QGT]).
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the inverse lifetime ($\eta$) which determines the width of Circularly Enriched Crystals (CECs).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that backscattering between time-reversed states maps the density matrix into distinct, symmetry-resolvable orbital contributions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the honeycomb lattice structure, the low-energy spectrum near BZ corners K and K', and show visualizations of the reconstructed QGT components ($\Omega_{xy}$) in various valleys.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by defining the need for tomography; it details the methodology using symmetry analysis on the $\hat{T}$-matrix approach; it presents numerical results confirming reconstruction accuracy against theoretical models; and concludes by establishing the technique's broad applicability to hexagonal heterostructures.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the core concept of reconstructing a full quantum state (density matrix) from limited, symmetry-averaged measurements mirrors challenges in characterizing open quantum systems where only macroscopic observables are accessible.
